item.title: Gunmen behead, burn 60-year-old man in Cross River
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar Gunmen have killed a 60-year-old man, James Edi Diwa, and set his body and motorcycle ablaze in Boki Local Government Area of Cross River State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 5:20pm along the Isobendeghe–Boje Road, where Diwa, a native of Katchuan in Irruan community, was riding his motorcycle when he was ambushed. The attackers allegedly shot him, beheaded him and set his remains and motorcycle on fire. The Cross River State Police Command disclosed this in a statement on Thursday by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eitokpah Sunday. According to the police, the deceased’s wife, Mrs Schola Abang, reported the incident at the Boki Divisional Police Headquarters on November 13, 2026, at about 6:10am. The statement said police operatives visited the scene following the report and commenced preliminary investigations. “The Cross River State Police Command has commenced an investigation into the gruesome murder of a 60-year-old man, identified as James Edi Diwa, who was allegedly ambushed and killed by unidentified gunmen along the Isobendeghe–Boje Road in Boki Local Government Area,” the statement said. The Commissioner of Police, Mr Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, condemned the killing and directed relevant operational and investigative units to intensify efforts to identify and arrest those responsible. The command said no arrest had been made as of the time the statement was issued. Ordue assured residents that the police would work to bring the perpetrators to justice. He urged members of the public to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their hands and provide credible information that could assist the investigation. item.title: 2027: ACF warns of emerging political violence, urges restraint
item.description: …Forum urges Tinubu, governors to ensure fairness to opposition By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has raised concerns over emerging signs of political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging political leaders, security agencies and Nigerians to embrace restraint and protect democratic values. The forum warned that provocative demonstrations, stone-throwing, abusive chants and attacks on individuals could undermine the country’s democratic process and heighten political tensions. In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Prof. Tukur Muhammad-Baba, the ACF described the development, particularly in major urban centres, as unacceptable, dangerous and condemnable. It expressed concern over reports and videos circulating in conventional and social media showing acts of provocation directed at politically exposed personalities and other high-profile individuals. The forum also condemned the use of physical violence, looting and arson to express political grievances, warning that abusive reactions to such incidents could further escalate tensions. According to the ACF, although political violence is not new in Nigeria’s electoral history, the country should have moved beyond practices that undermine its democratic development and contradict its societal values. It warned that political intolerance, incivility and disregard for law and order posed serious threats to democratic progress and the country’s future. The forum urged Nigerians to embrace calmness and civility, stressing that the legitimate way to express political dissatisfaction was through the use of their Permanent Voter Cards to vote in accordance with the law. It called on community stakeholders, socio-cultural organisations, trade groups, non-governmental organisations, traditional rulers, religious leaders and other citizens to intensify public enlightenment on the dangers of political intolerance and electoral violence. The ACF also urged political office holders, particularly President Bola Tinubu and state governors, to demonstrate fairness, equity and tolerance towards perceived or actual political opponents. It further called on authorities to ensure that opposition parties had unhindered access to public facilities for their campaign activities. The forum urged security agencies to respond firmly but professionally to emerging threats through coordinated and intelligence-driven measures. While commending the recent presidential pardon granted to citizens arrested in connection with the violence, the ACF said attention should now shift towards preventive measures to avert further incidents. It stressed that protecting democratic values and ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the 2027 elections required collective responsibility from political leaders, security agencies and citizens. item.title: I never planned to have two wives, 18 children – Veteran actor Oga Bello
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Adebayo Salami, popularly known as Oga Bello, has revealed that he never envisaged having two wives and 18 children, saying he initially wanted a simple family life with just one wife. The 73-year-old actor made the revelation during an appearance on the Talk to B podcast, where he spoke about his marriage, family and how life took a different turn from what he had originally planned. Salami said his initial dream was to have a small family, inspired by the marriage of his godfather, Femi Okunnu, whose lifestyle he admired. “I never planned to have a large family. All I wanted was a simple life with my wife, but life took a different direction. “Today, I see my children as part of my destiny,” he said. He recalled how he and his wife enjoyed spending time together, particularly having breakfast before he left for work, describing the arrangement as the kind of family life he had always wanted. However, he said his growing fame changed the course of his personal life and made it difficult to maintain the arrangement he had initially envisioned. The actor also recounted an incident in which two women gave birth to his children within the same week, describing the experience as overwhelming. According to him, he was making preparations for the naming ceremony of one child when he received news that another woman had also delivered a baby for him. Despite the unexpected expansion of his family, Salami said he had no regrets, noting that he now considers his large family part of his destiny. The veteran actor has two wives and 18 children, comprising nine sons and nine daughters. One of his children is popular Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo, and another named Tope Adebayo, who is also an actor. He also disclosed that he never imagined some of his children would eventually follow his footsteps into the entertainment industry. The post I never planned to have two wives, 18 children – Veteran actor Oga Bello appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: VeryDarkMan hospitalised in China after severe malaria scare
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Social media activist Martins Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan, says he nearly died after developing what doctors in China described as a life-threatening form of malaria. In a video shared on Thursday, the 32-year-old said he was admitted to hospital and placed in quarantine after his condition worsened. He said he had initially ignored a doctor’s warning and taken oral medication obtained through members of the Nigerian community in China. VeryDarkMan said he first visited a hospital where tests showed he had malaria. According to him, a doctor warned that it was a severe case requiring urgent treatment through his veins. He said he later contacted a doctor friend in Nigeria, who reportedly told him it was a common form of malaria. Doubting the Chinese doctor’s advice, VeryDarkMan said he left the hospital and sought medication. “Before I left, the doctor looked at me and told me, ‘They have to make things go through your veins. Oral is not going to work. It’s going to make it worse,’” he said. VeryDarkMan said the first medication he received had expired, so he asked for another dose. He initially felt better after taking it, but said his condition deteriorated that night. “My brothers and sisters, yesterday night, I swear to God, I nearly died, bro. No jokes. Exactly what the doctor said. The drugs turned against me. It became two times worse,” he said. He said he returned to hospital and was told to remain there. Doctors initially proposed seven days in quarantine but reduced the period to four days after assessing his condition, according to the activist. VeryDarkMan urged Nigerians to seek proper medical attention and called for greater awareness of severe malaria. He also appealed to the Federal Government to strengthen malaria prevention and mosquito-control efforts. Nigeria has one of the world’s highest malaria burdens. Severe malaria can cause life-threatening complications and requires urgent medical care. The post VeryDarkMan hospitalised in China after severe malaria scare appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Shehu Sani challenges opposition over poverty, insecurity
item.description: …APC chairman lists Uba Sani’s achievements, says governor has fulfilled campaign promises By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has challenged opposition politicians criticising the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, to account for their records in office, blaming successive governments for the poverty and insecurity confronting the country. Sani spoke on Thursday at the inauguration of the Kaduna State All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council and the flag-off of the party’s campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged residents to support the re-election bids of Tinubu and Uba Sani, arguing that those criticising the current administrations had previously occupied positions of authority but failed to deliver the transformation they now promise Nigerians. Describing the large turnout at the event as an endorsement of Governor Uba Sani’s leadership, the former lawmaker said the governor had demonstrated courage, conviction and commitment to development during his three years in office. He described the gathering as a reflection of the governor’s performance and a scorecard that deserved the support of the electorate. “Most of those making noise and criticising the government should tell Nigerians what they achieved during the years they were in power. The poverty we are experiencing today is a consequence of their failures. The insecurity we are experiencing today is also a consequence of their failures,” he said. Sani maintained that opposition politicians who had governed under both the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and APC failed to transform the country despite having opportunities to do so. “If they had the magic wand or miracle to transform Nigeria, they would have done so when they were in power. They were in the PDP, and they failed. They were in the APC, and they failed,” he added. He listed the appointment of three ministers from Kaduna State, the establishment of four federal universities, road infrastructure and efforts to promote religious harmony between Muslims and Christians among the achievements of the Tinubu and Uba Sani administrations. The former senator appealed to traders, civil servants, teachers, the poor and the wealthy to support the two leaders, expressing confidence that the APC would retain Kaduna State in 2027. Also speaking, Kaduna State APC Chairman, Atiku Isaac Sankey, said the inauguration of the campaign council provided an opportunity for the party to reflect on its journey, showcase its achievements and strengthen its political structures ahead of the 2027 elections. Sankey said the Tinubu administration at the federal level and the Uba Sani government in Kaduna had demonstrated that governance was not merely about occupying political offices but delivering tangible results that improve citizens’ lives. item.title: Joshua unable to see newborn daughter until after Tyson Fury fight
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Anthony Joshua says he will not meet his newborn daughter in person until after his December 11 fight against Tyson Fury, as he remains in training camp in Marbella. In an interview with The Sun, the British heavyweight described his daughter’s arrival as “amazing” and “a big blessing”, but said he wished he could have been present for her birth. He has spoken with the baby and her mother, Nicole, through FaceTime. “It’s not ideal but she is in good hands,” Joshua said. “She’s got an amazing mother, she’s got amazing family round her and the people at the hospital, I heard they were amazing. I spoke to them and said thank you, so I’m pretty content at the minute that she’s in good hands. But, for me, it would have been much better if I was able to be there.” The 37-year-old said he had committed to the fight preparations months ago and could not change his plans. “But I’m on duty at the minute and we’re on a mission. I knew about this nine months ago so I made this commitment that I can’t change, unfortunately, but there will be many more birthdays I’ll be at, for sure,” he said. Asked when he expected to meet his daughter, Joshua said: “Probably December 12, December 13. “I’ll go and check in and rock her to sleep, let her hear my voice and let her feel my heartbeat, really. The basic stuff.” The boxer, whose son JJ was born in 2015, said he intended to be a hands-on father. “I’m going to do it all. I’m going to definitely do it all,” he said. “You might see me with some eye shadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse just trying to do the right thing by her.” Joshua said he wanted to give JJ a sibling after the “painful and traumatic” experience of last December’s car crash in Nigeria, which killed two members of his team, personal trainer Latif Ayodele and strength and conditioning coach Sina Ghami. Joshua was also injured. “After the year that I’m coming off I wanted to do something positive,” he said. “I wanted to give JJ the opportunity to be an older brother. One day I won’t be here and he’ll have a sibling that he can turn to, be with and plan their future together. It’s nice to have a sibling that they can lean on each other when needed, when me and his mum aren’t here one day in the future.” Joshua said Nicole was healthy and described the birth as an “amazing experience”. item.title: 2027: APC governors have failed; no Rainbow Coalition in Jigawa – Sule Lamido
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Former Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sule Lamido, has criticised President Bola Tinubu and governors elected on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing their performance across the country as a failure. Lamido also dismissed the possibility of a Rainbow Coalition operating in Jigawa State ahead of the 2027 general elections. He made the remarks during an interview with Arise News on Thursday, where he discussed the political situation in the North, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), the party’s presidential candidate, Sandy Onor, and his son’s governorship ambition in Jigawa. Assessing the performance of the APC-led administration, Lamido said he believed both the president and APC governors had failed to meet expectations. “To me, APC governors nationwide have failed, like the president. That’s my opinion,” he said, adding that there was no Rainbow Coalition in Jigawa State. On the 2027 presidential contest involving Tinubu, Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, the former governor of Jigawa State described the political rivalry as a dispute within the same political family, noting that the leading contenders had previously belonged to either the PDP or APC. He also spoke about the PDP’s recent flag-raising campaign in Jigawa, saying the event had generated renewed enthusiasm among supporters who appeared eager to reconnect with the party. According to him, the reception reflected the people’s nostalgia for the PDP and their renewed hopes for its political future in the state. Lamido reaffirmed his support for the party’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, saying he would vote for him and encourage other party members to do the same. He maintained that his support was based on party loyalty, despite questions about Onor’s public visibility and limited campaign appearances. “You may not know him, but we know him, PDP. I know him. We know him, PDP. And therefore, I’m campaigning for him,” Lamido said. The former minister also challenged the suggestion that Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s political position represented the collective decision of the PDP. He argued that individual party members were entitled to express their political preferences, stressing that the party had not convened a meeting to agree on a common position. Lamido said the absence of a collective decision meant that the political choices of individual members should not be presented as the official position of the entire party. On the proposed Rainbow Coalition, he insisted that the group had no established presence in Jigawa and said he had not been consulted about its activities. He further argued that any decision concerning the coalition should be discussed and agreed upon through the party’s internal structures rather than attributed to individual members. item.title: Obi lists healthcare achievements as Anambra governor
item.description: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has highlighted investments in healthcare during his tenure as Anambra State governor, listing the construction of a teaching hospital, rehabilitation of general hospitals and expansion of primary healthcare facilities among his administration’s achievements. Obi disclosed this in the fourth instalment of his series, titled, “Nigerians, Go and Verify,” published on his X platform, where he outlined what he described as his administration’s efforts to strengthen the state’s healthcare system between 2006 and 2014. In the post, titled, “Building a Healthy Nation: Our Health Sector Record in Anambra,” the former governor said healthcare was treated as a comprehensive development priority under the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy (ANIDS). He recalled that when his administration assumed office in 2006, the state’s healthcare system faced challenges, including dilapidated health facilities, inadequate medical equipment, limited access to primary healthcare and accreditation problems in some medical training institutions. According to him, his administration consequently invested in primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare, medical training, maternal and child health, medical equipment and partnerships with religious and private institutions. “Our approach was simple: healthcare should be accessible to people wherever they live, and the quality of treatment they receive should not depend on their status or whether they live in a city or a rural community,” he said. Teaching hospital, College of Medicine Highlighting what he described as one of the administration’s major achievements, Obi said his government initiated, constructed, equipped and secured accreditation for the Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University Teaching Hospital in Awka. He said the project became necessary after he discovered that the state university was admitting medical students without having a teaching hospital to provide the clinical training required for their education. According to him, his administration constructed more than 25 buildings and provided facilities for the College of Medicine, laboratories, pathology, accident and emergency services, paediatrics, male and female wards, special wards and consultant clinics. He added that vehicles, including ambulances and staff buses, were also provided to support the hospital and the College of Medicine in meeting accreditation requirements. Obi said the objective was to establish an institution capable of providing specialist healthcare services while training future medical doctors. 15 general hospitals rehabilitated The former governor said his administration also rehabilitated and resuscitated 15 general hospitals across the state’s three senatorial zones to strengthen secondary healthcare delivery. item.title: Tinubu doesn’t need to rig 2027 election, Soludo says
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has declared that President Bola Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 presidential election to secure re-election, expressing confidence that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the contest. Soludo made the declaration on Thursday while speaking at a presidential campaign rally at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, where he argued that the APC had a stronger nationwide political presence than its opponents. “This election, to the best of our knowledge, is already won and lost. The president doesn’t need to rig any election. President Tinubu doesn’t need to rig any election,” he said. Explaining his position, the governor said the APC presidential ticket was facing opposition candidates whose political influence, according to him, was limited to certain parts of the country. “All over the country today, in every state of Nigeria, it is President Tinubu and Shettima ticket versus one other party. Whereas you have some other candidates who are strong in some parts of the country but don’t exist in others. “If you then take the totality of it all, do the arithmetic in your mind, this election is literally over,” Soludo said. He also attributed his confidence to the performance of the Tinubu administration, arguing that the President and Vice-President Kashim Shettima deserved another term based on their record in office. “President Tinubu, Shettima, they’re doing very well. They will win because they have done well,” he said. The governor further argued that the APC had presented a stronger policy agenda than its opponents, claiming that no credible alternative had emerged ahead of the election. “And let me put it on record, in terms of the agenda that they are pursuing, no candidate before 2023 presented a better manifesto, better agenda for Nigeria. “And so far, less than two months to go, no candidate has presented a credible alternative. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket presidency is on course,” he said. Soludo also defended the Federal Government’s handling of the economy and security, claiming that there was a consensus among people familiar with the economy, both locally and internationally, that the administration was moving in the right direction. He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, as one of the initiatives through which the administration was addressing the needs of Nigerians. item.title: Enugu 2027: Ohaa unveils tax relief, gratuity plans
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Enugu State, Sir Chinyeaka Ohaa, has inaugurated a 310-member campaign council and unveiled plans to provide tax relief for businesses, clear outstanding gratuity arrears and accelerate rural development if elected governor in 2027. Ohaa also promised to allocate 60 per cent of new road infrastructure projects to rural communities and improve security across the state’s 17 local government areas. He made the promises on Wednesday during the inauguration of the campaign council, chaired by Prof. Augustine Akubue, at the party’s secretariat in Enugu. The candidate also unveiled his manifesto, titled, “Rescue Mission 2027: Make Enugu Great for All,” with Hon. Johnpaul Ani named as campaign spokesperson. He urged members of the council to intensify grassroots mobilisation and expand the party’s support base, expressing confidence in their ability to secure victory for the NDC. Describing the appointees as tested and trusted party loyalists, Ohaa charged them to work harder to win the confidence of the electorate. He also urged residents to protect their votes and resist attempts by politicians to influence their electoral choices through financial inducements. Unveiling the manifesto, Ohaa said his proposed administration would prioritise economic recovery, institutional reforms, social justice, human development and equitable distribution of infrastructure across the state. On taxation, he promised to abolish what he described as unjustified daily levies, multiple taxation, arbitrary assessments and unauthorised collections, which he said were placing undue pressure on traders and small businesses. He proposed a unified business assessment system and a 12-month tax relief programme for eligible registered micro and small enterprises to enable them recover, expand and create jobs. The NDC candidate also promised to establish a Market Traders Recovery Committee within seven days of assuming office to investigate demolitions and document traders affected at Ogige Nsukka, Garriki, Holy Ghost and Abakpa markets, as well as the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium. According to him, the committee would assess compensation claims, provide emergency assistance where necessary and identify alternative trading spaces for affected businesses. On rural development, Ohaa pledged to direct 60 per cent of new road infrastructure projects to rural communities, establish 17 agro-processing hubs across the local government areas and provide 260 functional solar-powered water schemes, one in each ward, by the end of his administration’s third year. “The Rural Rescue Compact places rural communities at the centre of the state’s development agenda. Development must reach every local government and every ward, not just selected urban centres,” he said. item.title: Lagos-Ibadan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‍⁠‍‌⁠‌‌​Expressway: FRSC urges motorists to take alternative routes
item.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Ogun Command, has advised motorists to use alternative routes due to a gridlock on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The command’s Public Relations Officer (PRO), Mr Afolabi Odunsi, advised while speaking with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Sango-Ota on Thursday. Odunsi said the advice was to help motorists reduce travel time following the build-up of heavy traffic along the busy corridor. He urged motorists heading to Ibadan to consider using the Sagamu-Ijebu Ode route as an alternative. “Those heading to Lagos are advised to consider the Ikorodu-Sagamu route, where possible,” he said. He said the traffic congestion was caused by a combination of high traffic volume and ongoing roadworks on some sections of the expressway. Odunsi added that motorists travelling from Lagos to Ibadan were most affected by the gridlock. “The traffic jam reportedly stretched for several kilometres in both directions. “Also, many commuters are stranded for hours while trying to reach their destinations,” he said. Odunsi said FRSC personnel had been deployed to the affected areas to manage the situation. He urged the public to remain calm and cooperate with traffic officials as they try to ease the traffic. According to him, the command is working closely with other security agencies to ease the congestion. Odunsi admonished motorists against driving against traffic to escape the jam. He added that driving against traffic will only worsen the congestion and increase the risk of accidents. (NAN) The post Lagos-Ibadan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‍⁠‍‌⁠‌‌​Expressway: FRSC urges motorists to take alternative routes appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Pochettino calls for Man Utd to look beyond current struggles
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino says it is a “mistake” to dwell on Manchester United’s current plight, insisting the focus should be on the club’s potential as he prepares for his first match in charge. The Argentine takes his new team to bitter rivals Liverpool on Sunday — just days after ending his reign as US coach. United, who sacked Michael Carrick last week, are in the relegation zone after just one win in the Premier League this season. Pochettino, speaking to in-house media in his first interview as United boss, said he wanted to free up his under-performing players. “It’s a mistake to see the (current) situation,” he said. “We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. “But at the same time, we need to understand that it’s a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free. “The players need to express their talent, we need to create the environment and the platform for them to perform. That is the most important thing and that is the priority.” Pochettino will hold his first press conference as United manager on Friday. item.title: 2027: NDC campaign DG Abdulkarim accuses northern elites of entitlement
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has criticised what he described as a ‘sense of entitlement’ among some northern political elites, saying no candidate has the right to demand that others surrender their ambitions to Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 elections. Abdulkarim said this on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Wednesday while responding to allegations by African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Hajiya Najaatu Mohammed that Rabiu Kwankwaso was a mole in the NDC working for President Bola Tinubu. Dismissing the allegation as “their own imagination,” Abdulkarim criticised the way some politicians had approached the coalition-building process, calling some ADC politicians “lazy” because, in his view, they had not clearly agreed on the coalition’s purpose, presidential candidate or zoning arrangement before bringing people together. “I think that’s their own imagination. You see, I used to term some of the people I see in ADC as lazy politicians. Right from time, even when they are constructing this coalition that they talk about, instead of them to find a way of doing what maybe APC have done before, put everything in black and white that we want to come for a coalition, and this coalition, this is the person that we want to be the president, or we are zoning this part of what we are going to do to this part of the country, at that time everybody that is coming into that coalition knows exactly why he is coming,” he said. Abdulkarim said that setting out the terms in advance would make it clear why each politician was joining the coalition and prevent disputes over who should take which position as he questioned proposed plans to make Peter Obi Atiku’s running mate. “Immediately we started this, and they started to say that Peter Obi is a vice presidential candidate to Atiku. So what kind of coalition is that?” he asked. He also objected to what he described as an assumption that northern politicians should rally behind Atiku, saying Kwankwaso and other politicians had the right to choose whom to support and contest against. “And the entitlement from the elite, I find it very, very annoying sometimes. You just decide the North, which North? You talk like you earned something that you just put in your pocket, that anytime you want it, you just play the card of the North, and then everybody just follows that. These people have the right to contest election. There is no right given to Atiku, for example, to say everybody must surrender his for him,” he said. The NDC chieftain said Kwankwaso, who received about 1.5 million votes in the last presidential election, was entitled to decide where to go and whom to work with. item.title: Remi Tinubu seeks N70bn to complete National Library
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has said an additional N70 billion is required to complete the National Library headquarters in Abuja, disclosing that her 65th birthday fundraising initiative has so far generated N25.6 billion for the project. Tinubu made the disclosure on Thursday as construction work formally resumed on the long-abandoned National Library headquarters, a project conceived decades ago but stalled by funding challenges and repeated interruptions. The First Lady launched the fundraising campaign in December 2025 to mark her 65th birthday. She said the contributions came from wealthy Nigerians, women’s groups and other individuals who shared her vision of a world-class national library. While appreciating the donors, she acknowledged the challenge of raising the remaining funds, given the enormous resources required to complete the facility. She, however, urged Nigerians to contribute to the project, saying even modest donations would make a difference. “I have told the Minister that every contribution counts, even if it is just N10. Let everyone have an opportunity to say, ‘I contributed to the construction of the National Library’,” she said. Tinubu said the National Library was not merely a government construction project but a national monument belonging to all Nigerians. She urged students, individuals, organisations and other citizens to support the project, noting that collective participation would strengthen public ownership of the facility. Explaining her personal attachment to the project, the First Lady said libraries played an important role in shaping her life and deepening her appreciation of education. She recalled her years in the Senate, particularly during the 7th, 8th and 9th National Assemblies, when she consistently sought membership of the education committee because of her background as a teacher and passion for the sector. Tinubu said she and President Bola Tinubu understood the struggles associated with humble beginnings and believed education remained one of the most potent instruments for breaking the cycle of poverty. She recalled visiting the Qatar National Library in Doha in October 2025, where she saw how a modern library could serve beyond book storage to become a centre for research, technology, innovation, cultural preservation and lifelong learning. The experience, she said, reinforced her determination to see Nigeria’s National Library transformed into a modern knowledge institution capable of serving generations. She commended President Tinubu for renewing the government’s commitment to the project and urged contractors and consultants to deliver a world-class facility within the stipulated timeframe. The Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa, said the National Library headquarters, conceived and commenced in 2006, had suffered repeated setbacks before being abandoned for 16 years. item.title: Germany, France, Britain meet with Ukraine after Trump-Putin-Xi talks
item.description: Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Berlin Thursday for a “Coalition of the Willing” summit where Kyiv’s allies were to signal steadfast support and push for a European role in any future peace talks. The meeting – co-hosted by the leaders of Germany, France and Britain – was being held shortly after unprecedented three-way talks in China between US President Donald Trump, Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. The goal of the Berlin summit was to boost Europe’s role in any efforts to end the continent’s worst conflict since World War II, in a process so far dominated by Washington, Moscow and Kyiv. Zelensky wrote on X that “we are doing everything we can to ensure that Europe’s presence in the negotiation process is fully represented”. A so-called E5 core group – made up of Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland as well as EU officials – is expected to represent Europe in any potential peace negotiations. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff also arrived at the chancellery for the summit, expected to bring more than 25 European leaders as well as EU and NATO chiefs. The US envoys were expected to face questions on the China talks, where the three presidents agreed a brief “peace declaration” that touched on “strategic stability” but made no mention of the war in Ukraine. Putin, speaking later in China, said Russia had invited European officials, through diplomatic channels, to Moscow to discuss whether they should participate in US-led talks on ending the Ukraine war. “We understand that discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans,” Putin told a press conference. However, he also said Moscow could not accept any kind of military ties between Ukraine and Europe as part of a deal to end the war. Billions needed for arms Kushner wrote on X that he and Witkoff hoped “to further strengthen our close coordination with Ukraine and Europe, work toward a unified position on the key elements of a lasting peace, and to jointly prepare the agenda and proposed format for the next round of multilateral negotiations”. He added that the talks would also explore how the coalition “can contribute to post-war security arrangements, including credible guarantees for Ukraine and a broader framework that strengthens European stability and reduces the risk of future conflict”. Germany has emerged as the biggest provider of military aid to Ukraine since Trump scaled back US support and is also rapidly rebuilding its own military to deter a hostile Russia. item.title: Ebonyi gives shanty shop owners 15-day ultimatum to remove structures
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has given owners and operators of shanty shops at Quarry Junction, Abakaliki, 15 days to dismantle and remove their structures over safety concerns. The Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Chief Richard Ugo Idike, issued the directive during a routine inspection exercise aimed at ensuring compliance with urban planning regulations and protecting lives and property in the state capital. Idike expressed concern that the makeshift shops were located directly beneath high-tension electricity lines, describing the situation as a serious threat to traders, customers and other members of the public. He said the government’s intervention was necessary to prevent possible accidents, electrocution and loss of lives, stressing that commercial activities would not be allowed to continue in locations considered dangerous to public safety. The commissioner directed all owners and occupants of the affected shops to dismantle their structures within 15 days, warning that failure to comply would attract enforcement action by the ministry. He said the state government’s urban renewal and development agenda was not limited to creating a beautiful and well-organised capital city but also included ensuring that residents operated businesses in safe and approved locations. Idike reiterated the ministry’s commitment to regular monitoring, inspection and enforcement of building and urban planning regulations across Abakaliki metropolis. He urged residents, traders, property owners and developers to obtain the necessary government approvals before erecting structures or engaging in commercial activities. The commissioner assured that the ministry would continue to take proactive measures to prevent avoidable disasters and promote orderly development across the state capital. item.title: Treat gunshot victims first; police report can wait – IGP Disu to doctors
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, has urged hospitals and healthcare workers across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports, warning that delays could cost lives. Disu also called on members of the public to assist injured persons in accessing medical attention, assuring them that they would not face punishment for helping victims. The IGP made the appeal in a sensitisation message by the National Orientation Agency (NOA) in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, shared by the police on its X account on Thursday. Addressing Nigerians, police officers and medical personnel, Disu described the treatment of gunshot victims as a matter of life and death, stressing that no police documentation was required before emergency medical care could be provided. “Fellow Nigerians, I am here to address a matter of life and death – the treatment of gunshot victims in our hospitals. “To my fellow officers, to my medical personnel across the nation, and to every Nigerian listening, treating gunshot victims does not require a police report. “When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said. He urged doctors and other healthcare workers to prioritise saving lives rather than allow administrative procedures to delay emergency treatment. “To our doctors and healthcare workers, you are enjoined to treat gunshot victims immediately without waiting for a police report. Our duty is not to create fear but to protect lives. We wish to reassure citizens of their safety at all times,” Disu added. The police chief also appealed to Nigerians not to hesitate to help people who sustain gunshot injuries, emphasising that the law protects those who assist victims. “To the members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping. “Again, to my officers and medical personnel, please uphold the law because every second counts. Treat first, save lives,” he said. In a related message accompanying the video, the Nigeria Police Force warned that refusing or delaying medical attention for gunshot victims was punishable under the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshots Act, 2017. According to the police, the legislation requires all public and private hospitals to provide immediate treatment to gunshot victims, regardless of whether they have police reports or clearance. The police further warned that violations of the Act could attract imprisonment of up to 15 years and other penalties, depending on the offence. The law provides that every hospital in Nigeria, whether public or private, must receive and provide immediate and adequate treatment to anyone with gunshot wounds, with or without police clearance. It also places a responsibility on members of the public, including security personnel, to assist victims and ensure they are taken to the nearest hospital for treatment

item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Launches Worldwide To Near-Perfect Reviews
item.description: Gamers around the world got their first taste of “Grand Theft Auto VI” on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever. The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time. The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalized US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs. “GTA VI” launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time (1100 GMT Wednesday) and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight. New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. “Wasted already. First one, didn’t survive long,” he told AFP, laughing. “This is one of the big things in my life…I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time,” Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP. Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100. A 42-year-old gamer wrote on a German-language Reddit forum that he had taken time off work to play all night. By 1:20 am, he was already in bed with a headache, still blown away by the game. “Thirteen years ago, with a game like this, I’d have played until six in the morning,” the gamer wrote. In the game’s official Reddit forum, people raved about improved interactive elements, such as being able to push a stranded ski jet back in the water. “This is amazing!” one person wrote. Analytics firm Omdia estimates “GTA VI” could generate $3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive. PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored. People play Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at Bamboo Gaming Center & Bar in Bangkok on November 19, 2026, on the day of the highly anticipated video game’s release. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ In a review for The Verge titled “GTA VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype,” Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.” Social media users praised the graphics. “There’s one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human,” wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652. Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an “outlier” in the entertainment industry. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” he said. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter. item.title: I Will Rejoin Military To Fight Russia If Needed — Prince Harry
item.description: Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday. “I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend. “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.” Britain’s Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, speaks during the closing ceremony of the Ukrainian Invictus Games in Lviv, on November 15, 2026. Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics. The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham. “Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast. “I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added. Britain’s Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex (C) poses for photos with Ukrainian war veterans during the Ukrainian Invictus Games in Lviv, on November 15, 2026. Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv, he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”. He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”. The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army. Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William. But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online. Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images.
